name: Cryptocurrency footprint
seoDesc: Cryptocurrency footprint: work out hash rate from the social cost of Carbon. A free ecology calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: The Cryptocurrency footprint calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports hash rate immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. Think of it as a shortcut for a footprint, a resource or an environmental change you want to size up. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Cryptocurrency footprint calculator work?
sections.html:
The Cryptocurrency footprint calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports hash rate in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the considering the region as); then you type in the social cost of Carbon, the CO₂ emission per kWh of energy generated, the power Efficiency and the coin rewards in a block.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Cryptocurrency footprint calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Hash rate=(1250000000 ÷ 1251) × power ÷ power Efficiency
Time to mine a coin block=60 × with an exchange price of × coin rewards in a block ÷ network velocity
Your selected metal=energy required to extract a kg of metal ÷ having a market price of
Network velocity=3600 × power ÷ your selected cryptocurrency
Energy ratio=your selected cryptocurrency ÷ your selected metal
Time to mine a coin block=(3 ÷ 50) × energy required to produce a coin × coin rewards in a block ÷ power

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Time, opening in days
  • Mass, opening in metric tons
  • BTC – currency, opening in million
  • Energy, opening in kilowatt hours
  • Energy, opening in kilowatt hours
  • BTC – mass per energy, opening in kilograms per kilowatt hour
  • Mass, opening in kilograms

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Cryptocurrency footprint calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Putting a headline figure into context
  • Comparing two options on the same basis
  • Sizing an environmental impact in familiar units
  • Any time the same 1 figures keep coming back — the social cost of Carbon — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Cryptocurrency footprint calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns hash rate, derived from the social cost of Carbon. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Cryptocurrency footprint calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the social cost of Carbon, which is 17 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter having a market price of in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Having a market price of opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (5 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports with an exchange price of = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Cryptocurrency footprint calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
